title: Odisha Tender Rules 2026: The 14.99% Cap Is Gone
h1: The 14.99% cap is gone: how Odisha tenders changed in 2026
desc: What Works Department OM 173/W (3 Jan 2026) changed for below-estimate bids, and what 6,000+ results show since.
html:
Until the end of 2025, a bid more than 14.99% below the estimate was not allowed in most Odisha works tenders. In practice, many tenders ended with several bidders quoting exactly −14.99% and the work going by draw. In our 2025 data, 74% of decided tenders had their lowest bid at the cap.

Works Department Office Memorandum No. 173/W dated 3 January 2026 removed that cap, and OM No. 632 dated 9 January 2026 clarified it. Bidders who go deep below the estimate now give additional performance security in slabs linked to how far below they bid. Read both memoranda for the exact slabs before pricing a deep bid.

What happened next

The market split in two. Since January 2026:

  • Rural Works (CE RW I): median winning bid −0.1%, with 60% of tenders won at par (0 to −1%) across 3,566 tenders.
  • Works Department (EIC-Civil): median winning bid −18.6%, only 28% won at par across 676 tenders.

The same rule produced opposite behaviour. In crowded Rural Works tenders most bidders hold at par. In Works Department tenders with fewer bidders, discounts went well past the old cap.
faq: Is the 14.99% cap still in force in Odisha?
No. Works Department OM 173/W dated 3 January 2026 removed it; OM 632 dated 9 January 2026 clarified it. Deep bids now attract additional performance security in slabs.
Did bids go deeper after the cap was removed?
In the Works Department, yes: the 2026 median winning bid is −18.6%. In Rural Works most tenders are still won at par.

title: At-Par Tenders in Odisha: Why Crowds Bid 0% and How Draws Work
h1: At-par tenders: why crowded Odisha tenders are won at 0%
desc: How the number of bidders changes the winning bid in Odisha tenders, and what that means for your margin.
html:
In 2026 results, the number of bidders is the strongest single signal of how a tender will be won.

BiddersTendersMedian winning bidWon at par
1392−3.5%46%
21,196−2.0%46%
3–41,250−15.0%26%
5–7925−17.0%31%
8–151,358−0.2%54%
16+1,703−0.1%77%

With 3 to 7 bidders, contractors fight on price. With 16 or more, most quote at par and several tie at the lowest bid. 3,294 tenders in 2026 ended with a tie at L1; where the tie was at par, the median tie involved 15 bidders. The tie is then settled by the department’s procedure, typically a draw.

What it means for pricing

  • In a crowded at-par market, a deeper bid wins outright on paper but gives away margin that most rivals are not giving up. Know your break-even first.
  • In thin markets, the winning bid sits much deeper. Past results for the same office and size tell you how deep.
faq: How are tied lowest bids decided in Odisha tenders?
When several bidders quote the same lowest amount, the department settles the tie as per its procedure, typically by draw.
Why do many Odisha tenders close at par?
In crowded tenders, mostly Rural Works, most bidders quote at par (0%). With 16 or more bidders the median winning bid is −0.1%.

title: Reading a BOQ: Where the Money Goes in Odisha Tenders
h1: Reading a BOQ: where the money goes in Odisha tenders
desc: What 2,991 Odisha tender BOQs show about cost mix, concentration and local-material rates.
html:
We read the department BOQ of 2,991 open Odisha tenders. Across all of them, the value splits roughly as: Cement concrete 25%, Steel 17%, Bitumen / road surfacing 12%, Pipes & fittings 11%, Stone / aggregate 10%, Other 10%.

A few items carry most of the value

In concrete-structure jobs (CC roads, canal lining, culverts), about four items make up 80% of the BOQ value. Buildings are the opposite: it takes around 45 items. For simple jobs, price those few items very carefully; for buildings, no single material advantage decides the bid.

Local materials vary most

Processed items such as concrete and bituminous mixes are priced almost the same everywhere. Sand, GSB and stone vary by 25–40% between tenders, because the estimate adds carriage from the nearest approved source. A contractor with a source close to the site can price these items below the estimate and still earn more.

The estimate is the BOQ total

The published tender value matches the BOQ total almost exactly. Your discount is the gap between the department’s item rates and your real cost.
faq: Where do I find the BOQ for an Odisha tender?
On tendersodisha.gov.in, in the tender’s documents while it is open. After the bid submission date passes, documents can no longer be downloaded.
